# pulse_auth_settings (Resource)

The server's dashboard sign-in settings. There is one per server: declare it at most once.

Set `local_login_disabled = true` to make the dashboard SSO-only. Pulse accepts that only after an administrator has completed a test login on an enabled `pulse_sso_provider`, and while at least one enabled administrator has a linked identity on an enabled provider; otherwise the apply fails. While it is on, Pulse also refuses changes that would leave no administrator able to sign in with SSO. Break-glass recovery on the server keeps working.

Destroying this resource turns password sign-in back on (`local_login_disabled = false`), the safe default.

Import with any ID, for example `terraform import pulse_auth_settings.this auth_settings`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# SSO-only dashboard. Apply this only after an administrator completed a test login on an enabled
# provider and has a linked identity (pulse_user_identity); Pulse refuses it otherwise.
resource "pulse_auth_settings" "this" {
  local_login_disabled = true

  depends_on = [pulse_user_identity.alice]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `local_login_disabled` (Boolean) Refuse email and password sign-in, so people must use SSO. Default `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `auth_settings`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Any ID works: there is one set of sign-in settings per server.
terraform import pulse_auth_settings.this auth_settings
```
